title: Tanzanian Pigeon Peas
community: The coastal and Zanzibar pigeon pea tradition
author: Chef Fatuma
desc: Tanzanian Mbaazi — pigeon peas simmered in coconut milk with Zanzibar spices and tomatoes. The coastal Swahili bean dish that is eaten for breakfast on Zanzibar with mahamri — one of the island's most iconic morning combinations.
longDesc: Mbaazi with mahamri is one of the most iconic Zanzibari food combinations — the creamy pigeon peas in coconut milk alongside the cardamom-fragrant doughnuts. But mbaazi is equally eaten for lunch and dinner alongside rice. The pigeon pea's earthy, nutty flavour pairs magnificently with coconut milk.
steps: Cook soaked pigeon peas in fresh water 50—60 minutes until tender. Reserve liquid.
Heat oil. Cook onions until golden.
Add garlic, ginger, and spices. Stir 1 minute.
Add pigeon peas and ½ cup reserved liquid.
Add coconut milk. Simmer gently 10 minutes.
chefTips: Pigeon peas take longer to cook than kidney beans.
Add coconut milk at the end — never boil hard.
The earthy flavour of pigeon peas specifically needs coconut milk to balance it.
cookingScience: Pigeon peas contain more tannins than kidney beans — which contributes to their characteristic earthy, slightly astringent flavour. Coconut milk fat binds some of these tannin compounds, reducing astringency and producing a rounder, more pleasant flavour profile.
sustainabilityTips: Pigeon peas are drought-resistant and nitrogen-fixing.
culturalNote: Mbaazi with mahamri is one of the most celebrated food combinations in Zanzibar — the breakfast that Zanzibaris crave most when abroad. The earthy pigeon peas in coconut milk against the sweet cardamom mahamri is a contrast of extraordinary balance.
